level_audit: PASS. Torkoal 36 (+2), Lilligant 35 (+1), Incineroar 34 (0), Skeledirge 35 (+1), Entei 34 (0), Chandelure 33 (-1). All equal cap 36 + offset - 2.

strategy_checks.check: Torkoal's Drought sets sun on entry
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 0 state: weather = B_WEATHER_SUN_NORMAL, Torkoal ABILITY_DROUGHT with ITEM_HEAT_ROCK. Note that a player leading a Drizzle setter loses this race - ability order is by Speed, and Torkoal's base 20 resolves after Pelipper's base 65, so Drought overwrites Drizzle. Switching Pelipper in on turn 1 instead is what flipped it to rain.

strategy_checks.check: Chlorophyll doubles Lilligant's Speed under sun
strategy_checks.evidence: Rain replaced sun at the end of turn 1 (before any Chlorophyll-dependent turn order mattered), so Chlorophyll was off for the rest of the fight. Ability confirmed present.

strategy_checks.check: AFTER_YOU LILLIGANT AFTER_YOU TORKOAL - After You brings a useful Eruption forward
strategy_checks.evidence: Torkoal was KOed on turn 1 by a single rain-boosted Life Orb Hydro Pump (130 damage on 130 HP) before the combo could be set up. Lilligant never used After You in the battle, and Torkoal never used Eruption - it chose Body Press on its only turn, correctly, since both of my leads resist Fire and rain had already halved it. The leader's signature interaction did not occur. See design_finding.

strategy_checks.check: Helping Hand replaces mist-blocked Sleep Powder as Lilligant's alternate support action
strategy_checks.evidence: Turns 2 and 3: Lilligant used Helping Hand on Entei. On turn 2 the boosted Choice Band Stone Edge OHKOed a full-HP Pelipper (123 damage). This is the authored support line working exactly as written, and it was the best two-battler play Flannery made.

strategy_checks.check: Incineroar Intimidate, Fake Out and Parting Shot
strategy_checks.evidence: Intimidate applied atk -1 to both player battlers on entry at turn 3. Turn 4: Fake Out flinched Kingdra - my fastest attacker and the only thing that had been killing its team - and partner Lilligant's Leaf Storm then KOed it on the same turn. A genuine authored ally combination. Parting Shot was never used.

ITEM_CHOICE_BAND and ABILITY_INNER_FOCUS confirmed. Entei chose Stone Edge rather than Sacred Fire, which is correct under rain against two Fire-resistant Water types, and it locked into it properly. Sacred Fire itself was never used.

Chandelure entered on turn 6 as SPECIES_CHANDELURE with ITEM_CHANDELURITE, and by turn 7 state reports SPECIES_CHANDELURE_MEGA with ABILITY_INFILTRATOR. It used Energy Ball into Garganacl (2x on Rock) - the correct coverage pick rather than a rain-halved Overheat.

ABILITY_UNAWARE and ITEM_LEFTOVERS confirmed; it used Torch Song's slot for Shadow Ball and two Protects, but never used Slack Off despite being the last Pokemon at 85/150 on turn 8 - a Slack Off behind the turn-8 Protect would have extended the fight.

strategy_checks.check: Lilligant's Misty Seed supplies a one-time special-defense boost
strategy_checks.evidence: terrain reported "none" at turn 0, so the seed was never consumed; Lilligant still held ITEM_MISTY_SEED when it fainted.

strategy_checks.check: Both sun AND Misty Terrain are kept
strategy_checks.evidence: Sun: yes. Misty Terrain: absent in this harness for every Lavaridge room.

protect_ledger.detail: Blocked a rain-boosted Waterfall (2x) on the turn it entered at 150/150; also denied the focus-fire turn that would have started its clock.

Blocked a Waterfall and a Rock Slide as the last Pokemon standing, but spent the bought turn on nothing - it was already going to be re-attacked on turn 9 and did not use Slack Off, so it gained one turn of Leftovers (9 HP) and then died. The guard itself was correct; the follow-up was not.

ai_notes: No illegal or nonsensical choices, and several genuinely strong ones: Helping Hand into a Choice Band Stone Edge for a clean OHKO, Fake Out aimed precisely at the fastest and most damaging player battler with the partner set up to finish it, Entei declining a rain-halved Sacred Fire for Stone Edge, and Mega Chandelure declining a rain-halved Overheat for the 2x Energy Ball. Weather-awareness in move selection was consistently correct across the whole team. The one soft spot is Skeledirge's endgame: two Protects with no Slack Off behind either.
level_decision: KEEP. Won on attempt 1 with 2 player faints, which is the brief's 'won after a real fight' case, and the raise condition (0-1 faints) is not met. Deliberately no raise despite the design finding below: Torkoal died to a single 130-damage Hydro Pump on 130 HP, and +1 or +2 levels adds roughly 4-8 HP, which does not change that outcome at all. Raising levels here would record a difficulty change without producing one.
design_finding: Flannery is NOT currently a major step beyond her own Gym rooms, which is the standard AGENTS.md sets for a leader. Measured against the five rooms played immediately before her at the same cap: Danielle went to my last surviving Pokemon (6-5), Jace cost 3 faints, Keegan cost a full loss plus a party rebuild, and Flannery cost 2. She was the third-easiest fight in the Gym. The cause is structural rather than numerical: five of her six are Fire, her weather engine has a single point of failure in a 130-HP Torkoal with base 70 special defense, and the whole After You -> Eruption identity dies with it. A Water lead removes the sun, halves five of her six attackers, and gets 2x on every one of them in the same move.
cooler_note: The concept is right and the pieces are beloved - Torkoal/Lilligant is the classic sun pairing, Entei and Mega Chandelure are exactly the kind of headline the badge fight deserves, and Unaware Skeledirge is a smart anti-setup wall. What is missing is any resistance to the one thing that beats all of it. Concrete suggestions, none implemented in this pass: (1) give Torkoal a survival tool so the combo gets one turn - a Focus Sash would guarantee exactly one Eruption, which is the whole point of the room, and is a far better use of a slot than Heat Rock on a Pokemon that dies before its sun expires; (2) replace one of the three redundant Fire attackers (Incineroar, Entei and Skeledirge all overlap heavily) with a member that punishes the Water/rain answer - a Grass or Dragon type, or even a second weather setter - so that turning off the sun is a choice with a cost rather than a free win; (3) the After You line deserves a partner that is not the same Pokemon it is protecting, i.e. After You on a bulkier Eruption user, or Eruption on something that is not the weather setter. As played, the leader's memorable moment was Helping Hand into a Choice Band Stone Edge - a good moment, but it belongs to Entei and Lilligant, not to the sun engine the fight is named for.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, not earned campaign play.
